articles.title: EUA suspendem instalação de roteadores que levaram a apagão aéreo | G1
articles.standfirst: Apagão do espaço aéreo dos Estados Unidos causou a interrupção de todos os voos do país na sexta-feira (13). Investigações associam falha à instalação dos novos roteadores nos centros de controle.
articles.summary: Apagão do espaço aéreo dos Estados Unidos causou a interrupção de todos os voos do país na sexta-feira (13). Investigações associam falha à instalação dos novos roteadores nos centros de controle.
articles.body:
Passageiro observa o painel de voos após a Administração Federal de Aviação dos EUA (FAA) suspender a proibição nacional de voos em solo, no Aeroporto Nacional Ronald Reagan de Washington, em Arlington, Virgínia, EUA, em 14 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Eric Lee

A Agência de Aviação dos Estados Unidos (FAA, na sigla em inglês) suspendeu nesta terça-feira (17) a instalação, em seu sistema de comunicação, dos roteadores associados à pane que causou a interrupção de todos os voos do país na semana passada.

A decisão foi tomada após técnicos associarem uma falha em sistemas fundamentais de controle de tráfego aéreo a um desses roteadores — que tinha acabado de ser instalado em um centro de controle aéreo no Arkansas.

➡️ Na sexta-feira (13), a FAA ordenou que todos os voos dos Estados Unidos permanecessem em solo após uma falha em seu sistema de comunicação. O problema foi registrado em 17 dos 22 centros regionais de controle de tráfego aéreo do país. Como consequência, centenas de voos foram cancelados ou adiados, deixando milhares de pessoas em solo .

A FAA disse que também desativou novos roteadores, da marca Juniper, que já haviam sido instalados. Por enquanto, a agência seguirá utilizando roteadores mais antigos, da Cisco — em operação há 25 anos —, para manter a rede funcionando. Enquanto isso, seguirá investigando a causa da pane.

Os roteadores que apresentaram falha na semana passada estão sendo testados em um laboratório da L3Harris, empresa responsável pela instalação dos equipamentos.

Logo da NSA — Foto: Samuel Boivin/Reuters

Também nesta terça, a rede interna de comunicações da Agência de Segurança Nacional dos Estados Unidos (NSA, na sigla em inglês), usada para repassar informações altamente sigilosas, ficou fora do ar, segundo a rede de televisão americana CNN.

O sistema, chamado NSA Net, permite que funcionários da agência compartilhem informações classificadas como confidenciais. Até o momento, não há indícios de que a interrupção tenha sido causada por um ataque cibernético , disseram as fontes à CNN Internacional.

Enquanto tenta identificar a dimensão do problema, a agência adotou um esquema de chegada escalonada dos funcionários ao trabalho, segundo a reportagem.

Também nesta terça, relatos nas redes sociais afirmaram que o sistema de comunicação do Serviço Meteorológico Nacional dos EUA (NWS, na sigla em inglês) também saiu do ar, incluindo seus radares. A agência ainda não havia se pronunciado sobre os relatos até a última atualização desta reportagem.

EUA registram série de falhas tecnológicas

O problema na NSA é o mais recente de uma série de falhas tecnológicas de grande repercussão, que ganharam destaque no noticiário nos últimos dias. Não há ligação entre os episódios. Veja a lista abaixo:

Apagão na Microsoft : uma falha global nos serviços da Microsoft afetou empresas, governos e serviços de emergência em dezenas de países. O problema começou na quinta-feira (12) e persistiu até a sexta-feira (13), com falhas em ferramentas amplamente utilizadas no ambiente de trabalho, como o Outlook, o Teams e o assistente de inteligência artificial Copilot.

Apagão aéreo nos EUA : a paralisação de todos os aeroportos dos Estados Unidos , com pousos e decolagens interrompidos na sexta-feira (13). Uma falha no sistema de comunicação dos controladores de voo fez o país bloquear por mais de quatro horas o tráfego aéreo.

Falhas com bancos : grandes bancos dos Estados Unidos registraram problemas na última segunda-feira (16). Milhares de clientes relataram dificuldades para acessar contas bancárias pela internet após um problema técnico em uma instituição financeira provocar um efeito cascata no sistema americano.

Problemas generalizados na United Airlines : também na segunda, a companhia aérea enfrentou uma falha em seus sistemas que provocou atrasos em alguns voos . Segundo a empresa, o problema foi resolvido em poucas horas. Após a solução, a companhia esclareceu que não havia indícios de ciberataque.

articles.title: China ameaça retaliar contra EUA por restrições a chips de IA que também afetam o Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova regra de Trump exige autorização dos EUA para exportar determinados chips avançados a países como Brasil, Cingapura, Tailândia, Malásia e Indonésia; Pequim critica medida e ameaça adotar contramedidas.
articles.summary: Nova regra de Trump exige autorização dos EUA para exportar determinados chips avançados a alguns países.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com membros da imprensa ao partir para sua viagem às Filipinas e à China, na Casa Branca, em Washington, DC, EUA, em 16 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque

O governo da China afirmou nesta terça-feira (17) que se opõe firmemente à nova regra dos Estados Unidos que restringe a exportação de chips avançados de inteligência artificial (IA) e ameaçou adotar contramedidas caso Washington insista em aplicar a medida.

Segundo a agência Reuters, em comunicado, o Ministério do Comércio chinês disse esperar que os americanos retornem ao “caminho correto” e resolvam as divergências por meio de consultas e cooperação.

Anunciada pelo governo de Donald Trump na segunda-feira (16), a norma estabelece novas exigências para a exportação de determinados chips avançados de IA para data centers instalados fora dos Estados Unidos.

A medida busca impedir que empresas chinesas utilizem estruturas de processamento de dados em outros países para acessar esses componentes e treinar seus próprios sistemas de inteligência artificial.

O Brasil está entre os países sujeitos às novas exigências, ao lado de Cingapura, Tailândia, Malásia e Indonésia. Com isso, a exportação de determinados chips americanos para esses destinos passa a depender de autorização do governo dos Estados Unidos.

Os Estados Unidos querem evitar que empresas chinesas contornem as restrições já impostas à China.

Mesmo sem importar chips diretamente, essas companhias podem contratar serviços de processamento de dados em centros instalados em outros países. Assim, conseguem utilizar equipamentos avançados para desenvolver e treinar sistemas de inteligência artificial.

A nova regra busca impedir essa prática e ampliar o controle americano sobre o destino e o uso dos chips.

Isso não significa que o Brasil esteja proibido de comprar componentes dos Estados Unidos. A norma estabelece exigências adicionais para a exportação de determinados produtos, e sua aplicação depende do tipo de chip e das condições de cada operação.

Os chips avançados são considerados estratégicos porque permitem processar grandes volumes de dados e treinar modelos de inteligência artificial. Por isso, o governo americano tenta limitar o acesso da China a essa tecnologia.

A decisão foi anunciada durante uma viagem de Trump à Ásia, que inclui um encontro previsto com o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping.

A medida também é anunciada em meio a críticas ao secretário de Comércio dos Estados Unidos, Howard Lutnick, pela maneira como conduz as restrições à exportação de chips avançados para a China.

articles.title: Ataque em sites como Zoom e HSBC rouba cripto e infecta celulares | G1
articles.standfirst: Código malicioso foi identificado em páginas de 178 organizações, incluindo Zoom, CNN e HSBC; criminosos tentavam desviar pagamentos, capturar dados pessoais e explorar falhas em celulares da Apple.
articles.summary: O ataque cibernético em sites famosos atingiu 178 organizações e usou códigos maliciosos para desviar pagamentos e capturar dados de cartões e cookies de usuários.
articles.body:
Sites de algumas das maiores empresas do mundo foram usados em uma campanha de ataques cibernéticos para tentar roubar criptomoedas, capturar dados de cartões bancários e infectar iPhones. Entre as organizações afetadas estão Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce e IKEA.

Códigos maliciosos foram direcionados aos visitantes de sites de 178 organizações de diferentes setores. A ação foi identificada por pesquisadores de segurança digital e explorou uma falha em uma plataforma usada pelas empresas para melhorar o funcionamento de suas páginas na internet.

➡️ Os códigos maliciosos tentavam substituir os endereços de carteiras de criptomoedas pelos endereços dos criminosos.

Na prática, isso poderia fazer com que uma pessoa enviasse criptomoedas diretamente aos criminosos ao realizar um pagamento ou transferência, sem perceber que o endereço do destinatário havia sido alterado.

O ataque também buscava roubar dados de cartões de crédito digitados pelos usuários, capturar informações armazenadas em cookies — pequenos arquivos que guardam dados de navegação e ajudam a manter os usuários conectados aos sites — e fazer capturas de tela.

Além disso, os criminosos tentavam executar códigos capazes de explorar falhas de segurança em iPhones, que utilizam o sistema operacional iOS, da Apple.

A Reuters não conseguiu confirmar se os ataques tiveram sucesso nem quantos usuários foram afetados.

A campanha explorou uma falha de segurança na Optimizely, plataforma usada por empresas para testar e melhorar suas páginas na internet e a experiência dos visitantes.

De acordo com o pesquisador de segurança Scott Helme, os códigos maliciosos foram inseridos em projetos de clientes da plataforma e passaram a ser carregados em páginas de 178 organizações, expondo seus visitantes aos ataques.

A Optimizely confirmou o incidente. Segundo a empresa, um invasor explorou uma falha de segurança em seu serviço Experimentation para inserir códigos maliciosos em JavaScript nos projetos de alguns clientes.

🔎 JavaScript é uma linguagem de programação usada para criar funcionalidades e elementos interativos em páginas da internet. Nesse caso, os criminosos exploraram a falha na plataforma para inserir comandos capazes de executar ações sem o conhecimento dos visitantes.

A empresa informou que corrigiu a falha, removeu os códigos maliciosos dos projetos afetados, reforçou a proteção das contas dos usuários e adotou medidas para impedir a distribuição de novos scripts não autorizados.

Entre as organizações que tiveram sites associados à campanha estão empresas de tecnologia, bancos, instituições financeiras e varejistas.

A Salesforce , empresa americana de tecnologia, informou que estava investigando alterações não autorizadas nos códigos da Optimizely e desativou a ferramenta por precaução.

A Equifax , empresa americana de análise de crédito, também investigou o caso, suspendeu o uso da ferramenta e afirmou não ter encontrado indícios de que seus sistemas tenham sido comprometidos.

Já a IKEA , rede internacional de móveis, informou que estava investigando possíveis impactos sobre seus serviços digitais e clientes.

O HSBC , banco britânico, afirmou que não havia códigos não autorizados ativos em seus sites.

Apple , Zoom e CNN não responderam de imediato aos pedidos de posicionamento da Reuters.

O episódio mostra os riscos de segurança do uso de ferramentas de terceiros em sites de empresas. Mesmo quando seus próprios sistemas estão protegidos, uma falha em um serviço externo integrado às páginas pode abrir caminho para ataques contra os visitantes.

Ataques a criptomoedas já causaram bilhões em prejuízos

Os ataques contra carteiras e plataformas de criptomoedas continuam sendo uma ameaça ao setor. Segundo a empresa de análise de transações em blockchain Chainalysis, mais de US$ 22,3 bilhões foram roubados em ataques envolvendo criptomoedas desde 2021.

Em outubro, um ataque cibernético atribuído a hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte resultou no roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões da Binance, considerada a maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo.

Cybercrime; hacker; crimes digitais; crimes virtuais — Foto: Kevin Horvart/Unplash

articles.title: Cacique Raoni tem alta após internação por infecção pulmonar em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Aos 94 anos, liderança indígena apresentou melhora e recebeu alta para acompanhamento ambulatorial.
articles.summary: Aos 94 anos, liderança indígena apresentou melhora e recebeu alta para acompanhamento ambulatorial.
articles.body:
Cacique Raoni é diagnosticado com câncer aos 94 anos — Foto: Instituto Raoni

O cacique Raoni Metuktire, de 94 anos, recebeu alta da Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) do Hospital Regional de Peixoto de Azevedo , a 692 km de Cuiabá, no último sábado (15). Ele estava internado desde o início de novembro para tratar uma infecção pulmonar e controlar alterações na pressão arterial.

Segundo o resumo de alta médica, Raoni apresentou melhora e estabilidade hemodinâmica, sem necessidade de medicamentos para manter a pressão arterial. O documento também informa que ele estava lúcido e orientado no momento da alta.

Ele recebeu alta para dar continuidade ao acompanhamento médico em regime ambulatorial.

O cacique, que é uma das principais lideranças indígenas do Brasil e referência internacional na defesa dos povos originários e da Amazônia, é portador de uma neoplasia metastática e está em cuidados paliativos.

Em maio deste ano, Raoni foi internado no mesmo hospital após sentir fortes dores na barriga devido à uma hernia antiga, mas recebeu alta médica após dois dias de tratamento. Cinco dias depois, Raoni voltou a apresentar complicações de saúde e foi novamente para a UTI para tratar um quadro de pneumonia, onde permaneceu por mais sete dias.

Segundo a unidade de saúde, o líder indígena apresentava múltiplas comorbidades, entre elas Doença Pulmonar Obstrutiva Crônica (DPOC), cardiopatia com marcapasso implantado e insuficiência cardíaca.

Em setembro de 2022, ele chegou a ficar internado por cinco dias no hospital de Sinop, após ser diagnosticado com um problema cardíaco e passar por cirurgia para implante de marcapasso. Depois, passou alguns dias no município de Colíder até voltar para a aldeia.

Além disso, em julho de 2020, o cacique foi internado em um hospital de Colíder após ter passado mal. Ele chegou a ser transferido de avião para Sinop com complicações gastrointestinais e desidratação.

Em setembro do mesmo ano, foi novamente internado com diagnóstico de pneumonia pela equipe médica de sua aldeia, no Parque Indígena do Xingu. À época, recebeu alta médica nove dias depois. Ainda neste período, também apresentou um quadro depressivo após a morte da mulher dele, Bekwyjkà Metuktire.

O líder indígena é uma das vozes mais influentes do Brasil na defesa dos indígenas e do meio ambiente. Ele iniciou seu ativismo em 1954, aprendeu português, e foi uma voz importante para o reconhecimento dos direitos dos povos indígenas na Constituição de 1988.

🎬Raoni ganhou destaque internacional em 1977, quando um documentário sobre sua vida foi exibido no Festival de Cannes, na França;

🎸Em 1989, visitou 17 países durante uma turnê internacional ao lado do ex-baixista Sting da banda inglesa The Police;

🏰Em 2012, foi recebido pelo então presidente da França, François Hollande, no Palácio do Eliseu. Na ocasião, pediu pela preservação da Amazônia e dos povos que vivem na região;

📃Em 2020, recebeu o título de Doutor Honoris Causa pela Universidade do Estado de Mato Grosso (Unemat). O título é concedido a pessoas que possuem destaque na sua área de atuação ou que sejam personalidades respeitadas pelo trabalho com a sociedade;

🌳Em 2023, acompanhou o presidente Luis Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) ao subir a rampa do Palácio do Planalto;

⛪Em 2024, entregou uma carta ao Papa Francisco, durante um encontro no Vaticano, em Roma, para falar sobre as mudanças e catástrofes climáticas.

articles.title: Como aproveitar melhor as 93 horas da Black Friday da New Zone | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento acontece de 19 a 22 de novembro, com funcionamento ininterrupto, promoções relâmpago e estrutura preparada para receber clientes durante todo o período.
articles.summary: Evento acontece de 19 a 22 de novembro, com funcionamento ininterrupto, promoções relâmpago e estrutura preparada para receber clientes durante todo o período.
articles.body:
Quem pretende aproveitar a Black Friday em Ciudad del Este, no Paraguai, já pode começar a organizar o roteiro de compras. De 19 a 22 de novembro, a New Zone Importados realiza a Black Friday Furacão 24H, apresentada pela Garmin, com 93 horas consecutivas de funcionamento da loja, descontos de até 70% e promoções em diferentes categorias. A iniciativa foi planejada para oferecer mais flexibilidade aos clientes e turistas, que poderão escolher o melhor horário para visitar a loja e aproveitar as oportunidades ao longo dos quatro dias de evento.

A programação começa à 00h01 de quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, e segue até as 21h de domingo, 22 de novembro. Durante esse período, a loja permanecerá aberta também na madrugada, permitindo que os visitantes organizem suas compras de acordo com o próprio roteiro. Uma das recomendações para aproveitar melhor o evento é preparar uma lista de produtos de interesse e reservar tempo para conhecer os diferentes setores da loja.

Com mais de 55 setores, a New Zone reúne opções em tecnologia, eletrônicos, perfumaria, cosméticos, moda, esportes, artigos para casa e diversas outras categorias. A loja também conta com uma localização estratégica para quem vem do Brasil: é a primeira loja ao cruzar a Ponte da Amizade, a poucos passos da Aduana paraguaia. A variedade permite que os consumidores encontrem diferentes produtos em um único endereço, comparem alternativas e acompanhem as promoções disponíveis em cada segmento.

Outro destaque serão as promoções relâmpago, com descontos especiais divulgados em horários específicos ao longo do evento. Para acompanhar as oportunidades e saber quando cada ação estará disponível, a orientação é seguir os canais oficiais da New Zone Importados nas redes sociais, onde serão compartilhadas as informações e atualizações da programação.

Para proporcionar mais comodidade durante o período de maior movimento, a loja também contará com um reforço na estrutura de atendimento, incluindo mais caixas e espaços para guarda-volumes, contribuindo para agilizar as compras e facilitar a circulação dos visitantes. Os consumidores também poderão fazer pausas nos espaços gastronômicos disponíveis no complexo da New Zone.

Com funcionamento contínuo, variedade de produtos e uma programação especial de promoções, a Black Friday Furacão 24H é uma experiência de compras completa e confortável em Ciudad del Este, oferecendo mais tempo e flexibilidade para quem deseja aproveitar o período de ofertas ao cruzar a Ponte da Amizade.

articles.title: Novembro Roxo: superação e os desafios da prematuridade | G1
articles.standfirst: Davi Lucas e Sheila Karine: a história de mãe e filho que conscientiza sobre os desafios enfrentados pela prematuridade dos bebês.
articles.summary: Davi Lucas e Sheila Karine: a história de mãe e filho que conscientiza sobre os desafios enfrentados pela prematuridade dos bebês.
articles.body:
Davi Lucas e Sheila Karine: filho e mãe, exemplos do Novembro Roxo. — Foto: Clas Comunicação

“No dia 15/12/2025, tivemos a notícia que mudou toda a nossa trajetória e os nossos planos”. Este é o relato inicial da contadora Sheila Karine, mãe do pequeno Davi Lucas e esposa do servidor público Lucas Maciel, que conta uma verdadeira história de desafios e superação vividos pelos bebês prematuros e suas famílias. Davi precisava nascer, com apenas 27 semanas de gestação e pouca expectativa de resistir. Em 16/12/2025, às 02h56m, ele chegou com apenas 1.030 kg e ficou 257 dias internado. “Vivemos dias em que nossa fé foi testada, em que a comparação tentou nos parar e em que a ansiedade foi uma pedra no nosso caminho”, continua Sheila, hoje comemorando 10 meses de Davi, que cresceu bem e já pesa 8.1 kg.

Motivo maior das comemorações ao Novembro Roxo, campanha de conscientização sobre a prematuridade, que destaca a continuidade da assistência às crianças nascidas antes das 37 semanas de gestação, a trajetória de Davi Lucas revela a importância da assistência especializada e o valor do acolhimento durante toda essa jornada.

Segundo Sheila Karine a estrutura e a assistência neonatal fizeram toda a diferença para o tratamento. “Hoje na Unimed temos uma estrutura de UTI Neonatal excelente, com uma equipe multidisciplinar e um corpo de enfermagem que trabalha para além do profissional”, frisou. Para as mães de primeira viagem, Sheila aconselha estudar profundamente a prematuridade, seus riscos e desafios. Procurar os melhores profissionais e acolher o bebê com muito amor e cuidados. “Até hoje Davi Lucas recebe em casa periodicamente cuidados médicos com nutricionista, fonoaudiólogo, fisioterapeuta, enfermeiro e pediatra. Orientação e acesso à especialistas e apoio para acompanhar o desenvolvimento da criança, inclusive com visitas domiciliares do programa Unimed Lar”, concluiu.

articles.title: Multiple NEET attempts, weightage to class 12 scores: States' suggestions to Nilekani panel
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Several states have suggested allowing students to take the NEET-UG medical entrance examination more than once a year and giving Class 12
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Several states have suggested allowing students to take the NEET-UG medical entrance examination more than once a year and giving Class 12 board examination scores some weightage in admissions. The proposals have been made to a high-powered task force led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, which is examining reforms to national-level examinations, news agency PTI reported citing sources.The suggestions aim to reduce students' dependence on a single high-stakes entrance test. The six-member panel has received more than 50,000 submissions from students, parents, teachers, academic institutions, experts and other stakeholders."Certain states have proposed that NEET-UG should be conducted more than once a year to reduce the pressure of a single high-stakes examination. There are also recommendations that Class 12 should be given some weightage," PTI quoted a source as saying."The panel is yet to meet representatives from all states and seek their recommendations," the source added.Task force gets more time to submit reportThe Centre has extended the task force's tenure till January 2027. It was initially expected to submit its report by October 2026, but the government granted it additional time as consultations with stakeholders are still underway.The panel is examining ways to make national-level examinations more secure and prevent question paper leaks through the use of technology.Among the proposals being considered are a secure question vault, a large pool of questions prepared and verified throughout the year, and digital delivery of question papers to examination centres shortly before tests begin.The task force was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on July 26, 2026, a day after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister following widespread protests over examination irregularities, including the NEET-UG paper leak.The panel is headed by Nilekani. Its members include former ISRO chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.The panel was constituted in July to recommend reforms in the examination system following the controversy surrounding NEET-UG.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: China-US tech tensions flare ahead of Trump-Xi talks over new chip export curbs
articles.summary: China on Tuesday condemned new US restrictions on exports of advanced semiconductor chips, accusing Washington of using national security as a pretext to
articles.body: China on Tuesday condemned new US restrictions on exports of advanced semiconductor chips, accusing Washington of using national security as a pretext to interfere in global technology trade. Beijing also vowed to protect its interests and take any countermeasures necessary.The criticism came hours before US president Donald Trump was due to arrive in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, where he is expected to meet Chinese president Xi Jinping.The US Commerce Department on Monday announced new restrictions requiring licences for exports of advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, citing a “higher-than-normal risk” that the technology could be diverted to China.The rules, issued under an interim final regulation titled “Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors”, also seek to close a loophole that Washington says could allow Chinese companies to access advanced computing power through data centres located in other countries.Under the new framework, data centres worldwide will require US licences to provide large volumes of computing power using advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau and countries subject to US arms embargoes.Beijing accuses US of economic coercionChinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun accused Washington of repeatedly stretching the definition of national security and abusing export controls to target China's technology industry.“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Guo said at a news briefing.He added that China would take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.China's commerce ministry also expressed “firm opposition” to the restrictions, urging Washington to resolve differences through consultation and cooperation.It said the measures undermined market rules and the international economic and trade order, while threatening the stability of global semiconductor supply chains. The ministry also warned that Beijing could respond with countermeasures.Chip curbs add to tensions ahead of Trump-Xi talksThe latest dispute over semiconductor exports comes as Trump prepares to meet Xi during his visit to China. The two leaders are expected to discuss bilateral ties and broader geopolitical issues at a time when Washington and Beijing remain at odds over trade and technology restrictions.Trump is travelling to Shenzhen after attending the ASEAN summit in Manila, where he also participated in a meeting of Quad leaders alongside Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.The APEC summit, which brings together 21 member economies, is scheduled to begin on Wednesday. The Trump-Xi meeting is expected on Thursday.The new US restrictions also highlight the continuing contest between Washington and Beijing over access to advanced semiconductors, which are critical to the development of artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.Washington has increasingly tightened controls on the export of advanced chips and related technology to China, citing concerns over their potential use in military and strategic applications. Beijing has repeatedly accused the US of trying to contain its technological development.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: After years as a washerwoman, Madam C.J. Walker arrived in Denver with $1.50 in 1905; she built a hair-care company that grew to 5,000 sales agents
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring journey of Madam C.J. Walker, who rose from a laundress to a pioneering entrepreneur in hair care, creating jobs for thousands and transforming the beauty industry.
articles.body: In 1905, after years of work as a laundress to support herself and her daughter, Madam C.J. Walker set out for Denver, Colorado, with $1.50 in her pocket. What happened next was a business story that made her one of the most successful African American women of her era. She developed a line of hair-care products and sold them through a network of about 5,000 sales agents and stockholders.According to the National Park Service, Sarah Breedlove, born in Delta, Louisiana, in 1867, struggled with poverty and hardships early in life. Her parents, Minerva and Owen Breedlove, had formerly been enslaved and later worked as sharecroppers. She was orphaned as a child living in St. Louis, Missouri. Breedlove was a single mother and supported her child as a washerwoman. In her thirties, she began experiencing recurring loss of hair, which motivated her to experiment with commercial hair care formulas and create her own product.From laundry work to a business opportunity in DenverWalker's concern about hair care stemmed in part from her own experience. Widely available hair care products were inadequate or damaging, and many women suffered from scalp conditions and hair loss in the early 90s. Walker tested various solutions and eventually created one of her own that cleared up the scalp problem. She worked as a sales agent for Annie Turnbo Malone, a successful African American beauty entrepreneur, and learned the retailing side of hair care products by observing the Poro company.She moved to Denver in 1905, earning money as a cook and taking in laundry to sustain her small family. She gave the remainder of her time to making and selling hair care products door to door. Her early product line included Madam Walker's Wonderful Hair Grower, a vegetable-based shampoo that gained her a following in Denver’s Black community. Walker married newspaper salesman Charles Joseph Walker in 1906 and took the name Madam C.J. Walker. Her husband worked in advertising, promotion campaigns, and mail-order business with newspaper advertising and demonstrations, playing a vital role in marketing her products to customers outside her neighbourhood.Training women and expanding a nationwide sales networkWalker knew that growth would mean more than selling products. She would require a distribution network that could bring her products to consumers all across the country. She began by listing women as sales representatives, Walker agents, to demonstrate the products, perform treatments, and teach others how to follow her hair care regimen. The business also created the opportunity for women to start their own small beauty businesses out of their homes. Walker trained the women in product application and sales techniques, as well as operating a small business and keeping inventory and accounts. Many of the recruits were former teachers and women who previously would have had few employment options.In 1908, Walker relocated to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and created Lelia College, named after her daughter. The college trained women in beauty techniques and hairstyles, providing a handy workforce for expanding business. A more significant expansion happened in 1910 when the beauty magnate moved her operations to Indianapolis, Indiana. She opened a factory, beauty salon, and training school. Indiana had several freight lines radiating out of it and quickly proved attractive for manufacturing and selling her product to a national customer base. The National Park Service also noted that the network grew to 5,000 agents by 1910 and that the firm earned roughly $7,000 per week.A business legacy that extended beyond hair careWalker's influence and ambition did not stop there. In 1913, she opened a New York branch in Harlem, where a beauty salon and training school were set up to cater to the increasing number of clients. She moved to New York permanently in 1916, having already transferred the running of a manufacturing plant in Indiana to trusted employees. Her profits also supported educational charities and causes. She used her business to advance African Americans and encouraged the women who worked for her to take part in community service. Her annual conventions provided other businesswomen the opportunity to share experiences, discover new ideas, and build contacts.Research published in OAH Magazine of History also looks at Walker's business and J.C. Penney, a retailer, showing how each shared a different way of carrying out a business through sales, manufacturing, and customer interaction. Walker died in 1919 at the age of 51 and was succeeded by her daughter, Lelia Walker. She held her position until her death in 1931. Finally, in 1927, the Indianapolis headquarters became the Walker Building, a manufacturing business and cultural centre that represented C.J. Walker's ascent from a washerwoman with $1.50 to a national businesswoman.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Breaking Bad: Is the United States falling apart?
articles.summary: TOI CORRESPONDENT FROM WASHINGTON: There are days when the United States seems to be running the world.
articles.body: TOI CORRESPONDENT FROM WASHINGTON: There are days when the United States seems to be running the world. And days when it cannot quite manage to run its own email, banking, or airline reservation systems. From a nationwide grounding of aircraft and malfunctioning bank accounts to a suspected Iranian dirty-bomb plot, a succession of unnerving events -- while seemingly unrelated -- has put America on edge, fueling conspiracy theorists and comedians at the same time.The past several days have been particularly unkind to the country's self-image as the world's tech superpower whose leader has frequently disparaged "third world" countries. First came Microsoft's Outlook and other services going on the blink. Then the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered an extraordinary nationwide grounding of flights after a communications-system failure. Before passengers had recovered their faith in air travel, United Airlines suffered a widespread computer outage that briefly prevented departing aircraft from taking off on Monday evening, even as Chase Bank reported software problems disrupting transactions.If this were a comedy, the punchline would be that Americans could no longer reliably communicate, travel or access their money -- three activities considered routine in a functioning modern economy. But the laughter and self-deprecation in many quarters has been mixed with something more uncomfortable in others: anxiety bordering on panic.The timing has been particularly combustible because the tech troubles coincided with alarming intelligence reporting about a possible Iranian dirty-bomb or chemical-weapons plot targeting senior Trump administration officials in Washington. Suddenly, a series of apparently unrelated computer failures began acquiring a life of its own: Was America experiencing a run of bad luck, an infrastructure crisis, or the opening moves of a cyber attack?Influential voices amplifying the suspicions didn’t help. “When it looks like a duck, quacks like a duck, and walks like a duck, it’s probably a cyber attack,” former National Security Advisor Michael Flynn declared, warning that America's adversaries were probing vulnerabilities and asking if government agencies and private companies were communicating effectively. WIth apocalyptic gravitas, he suggested the U.S was already in a war in the cyber domain, compounded by what he described as a spiritual struggle between good and evil.On the flip side though, none of the organisations affected reported evidence of a coordinated attack. The FAA blamed its disruption on a malfunctioning router during telecom maintenance. The equipment, part of an aging network connecting more than 4,400 aviation facilities, reportedly flooded the system with repeated connection attempts, destabilising communications across the country. Microsoft attributed its problems to a technical issue during an upgrade. Chase said its disruption stemmed from a software bug in its hardware systems, explicitly ruling out a cyberattack. United, meanwhile, said there was no indication its outage was cyber-related and fixed the issue in a couple of hours.But facts have a hard time competing with fear when the failures arrive in rapid succession, addled by paranoia about distant wars coming home. CNN, citing seven US officials familiar with intelligence assessments, reported on Monday that Iran was developing possible plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon. The intelligence reportedly included specific locations and targets, prompting contingency planning. Adding to the angst, the Federal Emergency Management System (FEMA) scheduled a nationwide alert exercise on Tuesday – in normal times, a routine test when all broadcasts are interrupted for about one minute to check that emergency alerts can reach the public.This in turn triggered another sinister theory among administration critics: the succession of breakdowns and the heightened security threat could be used to manufacture a national emergency, expand presidential powers and justify extraordinary domestic measures, potentially including martial law. The basis for this suspicion? A President who had already tried to overturn an election, suggested the mid-term results were rigged, and has frequently hinted at a longer innings.Humorists and comedians provided some relief from the overwrought commentary, joking that America was running not on Windows95 but Windows1776. Jimmy Fallon, whose Sunday-night monologue followed the FAA debacle, took aim at the administration's explanation that outdated switches, routers, and copper wires were responsible while welcoming his guest Jennifer Lopez with the observation that she was there for the same reason as everybody else: her flight had been cancelled.For critics of the Trump administration chuffed by the mid-term results, this is also a question of political competence. They point to the administration's shifting explanations, its tendency to blame inherited problems on predecessors despite being in power six of the last ten years, and its apparent inability to communicate clearly or honestly during a crisis.For instance, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, a former reality star, has demanded $50 billion for FAA modernisation, even though he voted against some FAA funding in the past and claimed at a cabinet meeting with Trump a year ago that the FAA would be fixed by 2027 with the historic $12.5 billion funding from the big beautiful bill. Evidently, that isn't enough to prevent an ugly meltdown.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: University of Miami students Jasmine Rodriguez, Farzad Rezaeicherati, and Sevil Ozsut are turning Virginia Key algae into biochar for lower-carbon concrete, and their research has now won the $25,000 VoLo Foundation VISTA Award
articles.summary: Discover how University of Miami students are transforming algae into biochar to create lower-carbon concrete, winning the VoLo Foundation VISTA Award to advance their groundbreaking research.
articles.body: Algae collected near Florida’s coastline could help reduce the environmental impact of one of the world's most widely used construction materials. Three University of Miami researchers, Jasmine Rodriguez, Farzad Rezaeicherati and Sevil Ozsut, are converting locally grown algae into a biochar-like substance that can be incorporated into concrete to reduce its cement content while maintaining strength. Their research has earned them the 2026 VoLo Foundation VISTA Award, along with $25,000 to advance their work.The research, titled 'Functionalization and Pre-Carbonation of Florida-Native Algae Biochar for Carbon-Negative Cementitious Composites,' examines the potential for marine plant material to be used in construction. Led by civil engineering professor Ali Ghahremaninezhad, the students are trying to substitute some of the cement in an existing building material with biochar from algae and yet keep it strong and resilient. The award was made through the VoLo Foundation’s climate innovation program, which supported research conducted by students on environmental impacts.Turning locally grown algae into carbon-rich biocharThe algae they use are supplied by the University of Miami's experimental agriculture facility at the Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science campus on Virginia Key. They grow Florida native algae and use their local source of biological materials from the team's research. In the first step, they clean, grind and sieve the algae before transforming it into biochar by pyrolysis, which involves heating organic material to around 500 degrees Celsius in an environment with very little oxygen. During pyrolysis, the organic material is not entirely burned, resulting in a solid residue that contains carbon, much of which was absorbed by the algae when it was alive.The biochar produced can then be added to cement-based composites. But if too much untreated biochar is added, it can cause concrete to be weak, as the particles don't stick well to the cement. So the team are now trying to functionalise the materials, which means chemically treating them to change their surface properties to work better with the cement. The method also offers an alternative use for some of this local algae material. Coastal communities in Florida and elsewhere in the region frequently have trouble disposing of the large amount of algae that builds up in their area. Repurposing it into construction materials could be a solution in this case, though that is not yet available as a commercial waste management option.Chemical treatment aims to improve concrete performanceA key part of their work has been to change the biochar so that a large fraction can be added to concrete without degrading its mechanical qualities. The team is investigating the use of chemical activation to boost properties such as porosity, water absorption, carbon dioxide absorption and bonding with cement. Another step involves precarbonisation, where the biochar is first exposed to carbon dioxide before being mixed into the concrete. A third step is to use carbon while it is solidifying. This treatment promotes calcium carbonate formation, which locks the carbon away in mineral form.The team had investigated biochar for partially replacing cement in a different study, publishing their results and industrial applications and products. They explored how biochar could be used to store carbon, highlighting what workability and strength issues arise when it is used at higher levels. A different team reported in Construction and Building Materials that chemically functionalised biochar was capable of higher replacement levels, while also enhancing the mechanical performance in cement-based composites. This provides the scientific basis for the Miami team's algae-derived composite material and its intended use. The research team will need to determine the optimal level of treatment and substitution through the use of tests in the lab.$25,000 award will support the next stage of researchThe VoLo Foundation Vista Award will give the team $25,000 to further refine its technology and, hopefully, buy new equipment to let scientists better modulate the production of biochar and its properties. In addition to the effects on compressive strength and durability, the team is also investigating how materials perform in Florida soil, considering moisture and salt from the sea spray and humidity in construction materials.The production of cement accounts for about 8% of the world's carbon dioxide emissions. Much of that comes from the manufacturing process, which takes a lot of energy and the chemical reaction itself. So if concrete uses less traditional cement, that could cut the amount of emissions coming from the construction industry. But for now, the algae-based material is still being tested, and the team is working to optimise their processing methods and find the best replacement rate before working with industry to look at commercial possibilities.In the long term, they hope to create a type of concrete that uses less traditional cement, as well as sequesters carbon into a solid mineral. Carrying marine resources into the field of construction materials, the University of Miami team is taking a novel solution to the worsening environmental issues of algae overgrowth and concrete carbon emissions. The grant of $25,000 will help with further testing and implementationYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Kulgam op continues to track wounded terrorist
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Security forces intensified searches in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district Tuesday to track wounded TRF terrorist Mohammad Latief Bhat, who escaped
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Security forces intensified searches in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district Tuesday to track wounded TRF terrorist Mohammad Latief Bhat, who escaped after Monday’s gunfight that killed his associate and new recruit Umar Nisar Dar in Larnoo.Police sources said Dar had recently gone missing, prompting his family to lodge a report at Kulgam police station. He had allegedly assisted Bhat for months before joining TRF, a side-shoot of Lashkar-e-Taiba, after the attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam’s Mir Bazar on Nov 11 that left three personnel wounded. Dar and Bhat allegedly conducted reconnaissance at several locations, including Mir Bazar, on Nov 10.Bhat from Khrewan Chader village in Kulgam carries a Rs 15 lakh reward announced in Aug. He is accused of killing a J&K police head constable and two migrant workers in separate attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July last year.The prolonged search and restrictions across villages drew criticism from political parties. CPM MLA MY Tarigami, PDP politician Iltija Mufti and NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar accused security forces of subjecting civilians, including women, children and elderly people, to indiscriminate frisking and harassment. They said action against those responsible for the attack should not cause hardship to innocent residents.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Dracula' star Bela Lugosi once rented this Hollywood mansion, nicknamed his 'daytime coffin'; the 1929 Spanish Revival villa, later owned by songwriter Jimmy Van Heusen, has sold for $6.75 million
articles.summary: Villa Dorada, a 1929 Spanish Revival home in the Outpost Estates community of Los Angeles, came to market in September 2025 for $7.5 million, its first
articles.body: Villa Dorada, a 1929 Spanish Revival home in the Outpost Estates community of Los Angeles, came to market in September 2025 for $7.5 million, its first listing in more than 50 years. Lugosi, who died in 1956 and became famous for playing the villainous vampire in the 1931 classic Dracula, rented the villa in the early 1930s. The three-storey house covers 7,400 square feet and has six bedrooms, a grand ballroom and a three-car garage. Original features survive throughout, including magnesite floors, hand-carved wooden doors and a wood-panelled elevator, all outlasting a succession of owners.From Lugosi’s ‘daytime coffin’ to Van Heusen’s rumoured Sinatra hangout; who lived at Villa DoradaAccording to the Realtor, the villa later passed to Oscar-winning songwriter Jimmy Van Heusen, a close friend of Frank Sinatra who wrote “Come Fly With Me” and owned the house in the 1950s. The villa was originally commissioned by Minneapolis physician Frederick A. Dunsmoor and rented to Lugosi by its owner, Elizabeth D. Clark, at the height of his Dracula fame, earning it a reputation as the actor’s “daytime coffin”. Heiress Elizabeth Stack, daughter of “Unsolved Mysteries” host Robert Stack, bought it in 1946 and lived there for seven years before it passed to Van Heusen in 1953, four years before he won the second of his four Academy Awards. He sold it in 1957, and it changed hands several more times before the owner who listed it bought it in 1972. Sinatra is rumoured to have been a guest, and some suggest the house served as a bachelor pad for him, Van Heusen and their writing partner Sammy Cahn.Ornate tiling, beamed ceilings and a telephone room; inside Bela Lugosi’s former rentalThe listing describes ornate tiling around the fireplaces, beamed ceilings, curving wooden built-ins, tiled stairs with a painted ceiling above them and Art Deco brass doorknobs. Floors combine hardwood with magnesite, a type of concrete. The formal living room has space for a piano, a fireplace and a terrace, while the primary suite adds a fireplace, a sitting area, two balconies and a marble-drenched bathroom. Other spaces include a telephone room, a step-down parlour with a built-in bar and powder room, and a two-bedroom apartment with its own living room. Outside is a grassy lawn with a small pond. The kitchen has dark wood cabinetry, an island with a cooking range and a breakfast nook, though its tiling may date to the 1970s and future owners will likely want to update it.The commissioned history that uncovered the house’s rare ‘Extra Special’ construction ratingThe owner who listed the villa commissioned a thorough history of the house, which listing agent John Zaffarano told Realtor became a key part of the sale. Zaffarano said the research uncovered original permits awarding the highest Builder Assessor ratings of the era: “Special” for plumbing and electrical fixtures, and the rare “Extra Special” for overall construction, which he said affirms exceptional craftsmanship.The villa sits on a flat cul-de-sac in Outpost Estates, one of the Hollywood Hills’ most coveted communities, with views stretching from the Hollywood Sign to Downtown Los Angeles and the Pacific Ocean. Neighbours have included Brad Pitt, Charlize Theron, Orlando Bloom and Winona Ryder, and Pitt had bought a Spanish-style home nearby for roughly $12 million from Dave Keuning, lead guitarist of The Killers. Tom Davila, a listing agent with Compass, told Mansion Global in an email that he had lived in the community for 30 years and loved the carob trees lining Outpost Drive, and that the neighbourhood was one of the few late-1920s developments to bury all utilities, keeping the views free of poles and wires. As per RARE Properties, the villa was sold for $6,750,000 against the house, below the $7.5 million originally asked.Disclaimer: Every fact, figure and quotation in this article is taken from, and credited to, the sources named within it. None of the information is the writer’s own assumption, inference or insinuation.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: ‘Explain Chorbagan media briefing’: Medical College serves notice on 8 interns, asks them to give reasons within 3 days on why they were not on duty at the time
articles.summary: Eight Kolkata Medical College interns face show-cause notices for a late-night press meet after Chorbagan stampede, asked to explain duty absence and remarks.
articles.body: Kolkata: Eight Medical College interns who had held a news conference while victims of Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal stampede were admitted to the hospital have been served a show-cause notice and asked to explain within three days why they were not on duty at the time and why disciplinary action should not be initiated against them.The show-cause letter, signed by the principal of Medical College, states: “Interns of Medical College, Kolkata gave press briefings before the electronic media, accusing inadequacy of infrastructure and non-availability of certain drugs like Tranexamic acid and syringes, including clot vials, at that time... Why were you not on duty at that time? Why further disciplinary action should not be initiated against you?”On Saptami evening, a stampede at Chorbagan claimed 19 lives and left 25 injured. With many of the injured patients getting shifted from Medical College to Apollo Multispecialty Hospitals, a section of interns had come to criticise the move. The interns’ news conference came at 2 am, around five hours after the incident.Asked about the show-cause, state health minister Sharadwat Mukhopadhyay said, “Work in compliance with law is not revenge. If interns are found to have violated rule, an action will be taken following NMC guidelines.”Medical organisations criticised the show-cause notices. Biplab Chandra, state secretary of Medical Service Centre, said, “The interns have been show-caused for raising voice against the sorry state of infrastructure in Medical College. We condemn this.”Three interns TOI spoke to claimed they had gone to help in the emergency ward on Oct 17 “voluntarily” even though they were not on duty at the time. “I was in the hostel. Having heard of the incident, I rushed to the emergency where the victims were brought, and assisted my colleagues. I shall inform the college authority about this in my response to the show-cause,” said an intern. The other five claimed they had not convened the news conference at the cost of duty.Another intern said, “When the process of shifting the injured pandal hoppers to a private facility started, we held the news conference. No patient had to face any problem. Heads of medical departments and PGTs were present.”One of the interns claimed Mukhopadhyay himself had asked patients’ families whether they wanted transfers from Medical College to a private facility. “In a way, it was an admission from the minister that Medical College is not fit to deliver the required care and services. How can patients be transferred from this hospital?” the intern asked.The show-cause letter says the allegations made by interns were false. “This misinformation defamed the govt as well as caused impairment in the proper delivery of emergency care services by creating a commotion in front of the Emergency Gate,” the letter reads.Citing NMC regulations, the letter goes on to state, “Giving a press statement while on duty is an offence and an act of indiscipline.” The National Medical Commission (Compulsory Rotating Medical Internship) Regulations, 2021 provide for “curtailing or temporarily suspending or cancellation of internship by the institution/university if there are proven acts of indiscipline or there are proven acts of professional misconduct”.Earlier, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari had warned, “Holding a press meet during duty hours goes against service rule. A disciplinary action will be taken.”At a previous meeting, Mukhopadhyay alleged that some groups across medical colleges were running illegal rackets in which interns’ assigned duties or night shifts were sold to others in exchange for money.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: US, Iran exchange fire despite talks with mediators
articles.summary: DUBAI, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US mil...
articles.body:
By Nayera Abdallah, Jana Choukeir and Phil Stewart

DUBAI, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.

The latest back-and-forth between the US and Iran ‌was a reminder of difficulties ending nearly nine months of war that have destabilised the Middle East, pushed up global energy prices and fueled US voter anger in November ‌elections that punished President Donald Trump's Republican Party.

A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said US fighter jets fired on a Revolutionary Guards missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz in response to Iran's "aggression targeting ​US personnel and assets." Iranian media, citing an Iranian official, said the US attack did not damage infrastructure.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier on Tuesday they targeted a US military radar system at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa base, and warned Bahrain over its alliance with the US and stance towards Shi'ite clergy.

Bahrain, which is home to the headquarters of the US Fifth Fleet, said it intercepted the attack and there were no reports of casualties or damage.

Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday for talks aimed at "bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground," Qatari spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said.

They coincide with a visit to ‌Oman by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. Oman's Foreign Ministry said he ⁠discussed safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of global shipping and trade, as well as preventing military escalation, with Oman's foreign minister.

Oman and Iran lie on opposite sides of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway that carried about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies before ⁠the war but is now partly blocked by Iran.

Oman has previously held talks with Tehran about controlling traffic in the strait.

Araqchi said in a post on Telegram that he also met Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq and informed him about Iran's diplomatic initiative to end the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

The war has ground to a stalemate, with Trump saying he might ​hold ​off from attacking Iran if the US does not face what he described as provocations from Tehran or the ​Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen.

Trump said on Tuesday the US was taking seriously ‌the possibility that Iran could be planning an attack involving a dirty bomb in Washington, after being asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said the report was part of a US campaign "to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs" using "baseless allegations."

Trump has also said he will maintain a US naval blockade on Iran because it has continued to disrupt shipping in the strait, which is a sticking point in negotiations.

Attacks on tankers have increased this month in the strait, and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the crew of a tanker passing through the waterway was unaccounted for after being attacked north of the Omani port city of Khasab.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards and navy said on Tuesday that a ship carrying LNG and two oil tankers ‌had caught fire in the strait. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.

Benchmark Brent crude futures were up 0.4% ​at $92.76 a barrel, much higher than before the war but well below April's wartime peak of $126.41.

The war continues to spill ​over into other parts of the Middle East as Iran puts pressure on Washington ​through its Houthi allies, who have carried out attacks on Saudi Arabia and seized areas along the Yemeni coast on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, hoping to squeeze Gulf ‌oil producers.

Tuesday's attack on Bahrain, a Shi'ite-majority country ruled by a Sunni ​Muslim family, followed the sentencing there of 64 people, ​mostly Shi'ite clerics, to life in prison on charges of colluding with Iran to undermine the state.

Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the court's ruling on Tuesday and said the accusations were baseless. Tehran has long denied interference in Bahrain's internal affairs.

Iran also fired on Bahrain on Sunday, saying it had targeted a US radar system at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base following what ​it said were hostile US actions.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi ‌said Bahrain had made "three key mistakes," which he listed as "cooperating in the invasion of the Islamic Republic of Iran, remaining within the US security bubble, and encroaching on the ​sanctity of Shi'ite religious authority."

These, "if continued, will jeopardize its survival in the region's new security order," Mohebbi said.

(Additional reporting by Yomna Ehab and Elwely Elwelly, Writing by ​Nayera Abdallah, Aidan Lewis and Phil Stewart; Editing by Ros Russell, Peter Graff, Don Durfee and Rod Nickel)

articles.title: After govt push, curbs on sexual post recommendations on Instagram
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Meta has tightened Instagram's recommendations in India, disclosing the changes a month after the govt asked it to review how Instagram and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Meta has tightened Instagram's recommendations in India, disclosing the changes a month after the govt asked it to review how Instagram and Facebook suggest posts. Meta said Instagram now recommends fewer sexually suggestive posts and depictions of violence.The changes apply to suggested posts from accounts users do not follow, including in Reels, and the main feed. Posts complying with Instagram's rules can remain on the platform even if they are excluded from recommendations.Meta said it had strengthened its default safeguards over the past year based on user feedback. Instagram uses AI models to assess posts before recommending them and has fine-tuned its systems for India to identify more sensitive material."We've seen people report recommended content about half as often as they were a year ago," Meta said in a blog post. The company did not disclose the underlying figures.In its Oct 10 advisory, the IT ministry asked Meta to review how it ranks and recommends posts, citing concerns that its systems could give undue prominence to misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material. It also sought stronger checks on posts that could incite violence or disrupt public order.The IT ministry asked Meta to ensure that users were not disproportionately exposed to a narrow set of narratives and to report back on the steps it had taken. Meta did not link the Instagram changes to the advisory or say whether it had changed how either platform recommends posts about events in India.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: SC upholds stay on Azam Khan's conviction; offers son, wife relief
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday upheld Allahabad HC's order staying the conviction of SP neta Azam Khan in a case relating to the forgery of a birth
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday upheld Allahabad HC's order staying the conviction of SP neta Azam Khan in a case relating to the forgery of a birth certificate and granted the same relief to Khan's son and wife, who were denied this benefit by the high court.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said all three were on the same footing and questioned the HC for discriminating among them. It said there was "apparent legal dichotomy in the judgement". It said, "We find that the HC failed to articulate any coherent legal reason why similar relief, as granted to Mohammad Azam Khan, was denied, even though all three were convicted under the self-same charge of conspiracy.""Where several convicts standing on the same footing seek stay/suspension of conviction, it is legitimate for them to expect similar treatment... Parity being a facet of Article 14 of Constitution, equals ought to be treated equally unless, of course, an intelligible differentia having a rational nexus with the object of the order distinguishes one from the others," the bench said.SC said though differential treatment was not forbidden, "an unreasoned differential treatment cannot be sustained". It said, "If the court grants a stay/suspension of conviction to one... while similar relief to other similarly situated convicts is denied, the distinguishing feature on the record must be identified and expressly stated as the reason for the departure from parity. An order silent on that point is, by itself, arbitrary."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Leo Shani Horoscope Today, 18 November 2026: Sun Square Jupiter, and Shani Brings Back a Teacher’s Guidance
articles.summary: Advice from someone who once taught you may prove timely for Leo this Wednesday.
articles.body: Advice from someone who once taught you may prove timely for Leo this Wednesday. The Sun, your ruling planet, travels through Scorpio, your fourth house, and squares Jupiter, the planet of teachers and wisdom, which sits in your own sign beside Mars and Ketu. This tense angle can make you feel very sure of your views, sometimes too sure. Shani, retrograde in Pisces, your eighth house, has a way of bringing the past back for review. A former teacher, mentor or elder’s words may return through memory, a message or an unexpected meeting, and they may correct your course.When Confidence Needs a CheckJupiter in your first house gives you strong beliefs and a sense of purpose. The Sun’s square from your fourth house can create tension between your public confidence and your private doubts. You might be planning a big move, defending an opinion at home or dismissing advice from family.Pause before insisting you are right. A wiser voice may see what you cannot.Shani Returns an Old LessonShani in your eighth house, during your Dhaiya, governs hidden knowledge and lessons learned through hardship. In retrograde, it will often bring back something you learned long ago but forgot. Perhaps a teacher once cautioned you about impatience or a mentor advised you to save before you spend. Suddenly, that lesson may feel relevant today.Partners Offer Another PerspectiveThe Moon moves through Shatabhisha in Aquarius, your seventh house, alongside Rahu. A spouse or business partner may echo the same advice your teacher once gave. Listen even if their tone feels sharp. Shatabhisha favours healing through truth.Clearer Words for the Week AheadMercury moves direct in Libra, your third house of communication, and it is Mercury’s own weekday. Reaching out to a former teacher by call or message goes smoothly today. Venus, direct in Virgo, your second house, helps you speak respectfully even when you disagree.What to Do TodayBefore making a big decision, think about what a respected teacher or mentor would advise. If a partner or elder asks you about your plan, listen calmly. Reach out to a former teacher if they come to mind. Avoid insisting on being right in family discussions. Write down any lesson you recall so you can use it later.Shani Remedy for TodayOffer yellow flowers before an image of Lord Dakshinamurthy, Shiva's form as the supreme teacher, and pray for humility. Invite a former teacher or retired mentor for a meal at your home this week.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.body: The Earthshot Prize Summit concluded Tuesday night with a star-studded awards ceremony at Mumbai's Jio World Convention Centre, attended by Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis, Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Sonam Kapoor and Oscar-winning actor Rami Malek.The Prince and Princess of Wales were among the biggest draws. But it was India's Mahindra Last Mile Mobility that brought the house down, winning the Clean Our Air prize for driving India's electric three-wheeler market. Its managing director and CEO Suman Mishra said the company's efforts had shown that economic progress and sustainable climate action could coexist. Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A 62-year-old son fought his siblings for their parents’ £600,000 home, claiming he was promised the entire inheritance; a judge rejected his account, ordered him to leave within 28 days and pay £265,000
articles.summary: A family home worth around £600,000 became the centre of a prolonged inheritance dispute after one of three siblings attempted to secure the property for
articles.body: A family home worth around £600,000 became the centre of a prolonged inheritance dispute after one of three siblings attempted to secure the property for himself. Robert Chung, 62, argued that his parents had intended him to receive the house because he had returned to live with them and claimed to have cared for them in their later years. His brother and sister, however, painted a different picture, accusing him of behaving like a 'parasite' by relying on their mother to look after him rather than providing care in return. They challenged his account of the family's arrangements and disputed his claim to the entire inheritance. As reported by The Independent, the dispute eventually reached Central London County Court, where a judge rejected his claims, directed him to leave the property and ordered him to pay £265,000 in costs and occupation-related charges.How the £600,000 family home became the centre of an inheritance disputeRobert's parents, Victor and Irene Chung, raised their three children in a detached, three-bedroom house in Mulberry Way, South Woodford. The property later became the most valuable part of their estate. While Robert's siblings, Marina Bennett and Richard Chung, moved away and established professional careers, he remained closely connected to the family home.Robert had previously moved out to Berkshire but returned in 1990. He subsequently worked at a Job Centre and continued living with his parents. His father died in 1998, leaving his estate to Irene. When she died in 2016, she had not left a will. Under the rules governing intestacy, her estate was therefore to be divided equally among her three children.Robert disputed the arrangement. He maintained that his parents had told him he would eventually receive the house, claiming that his decision to return home had been connected to providing support as they grew older. His siblings rejected this version of events, arguing that there was no reliable evidence of any agreement that would entitle him to the entire property.Robert claimed his parents promised him the entire family homeDuring the proceedings, Robert told the court that his father had assured him he would inherit the family home. He also alleged that Victor had said Irene could return to Finland, where she was originally from, without receiving any part of his estate. Robert claimed that his mother repeated the promise after her husband's death, giving him further reason to believe the property would eventually belong to him.His siblings disputed these assertions. Their legal representative, Faisel Sadiq, argued that the parents had not made any such commitment and that Robert's attempt to obtain the entire property would leave little of the inheritance for Marina and Richard.The judge also considered the documentary evidence, including Victor's final will, which left his estate to Irene. There was no reference to the alleged arrangement concerning the house or to any intention to exclude his wife from the inheritance. Recorder Lawrence McDonald found Robert's account unreliable. He said several parts of his evidence were inconsistent with other material presented during the case and that some of his claims had emerged only when he was questioned in court.The judge rejected the suggestion that Victor had intended to leave his wife without financial provision after their decades-long marriage. He concluded that Robert had lied about the alleged promises made by both parents.Siblings challenged his claims of caring for their elderly motherThe disagreement was not limited to who should inherit the property. A significant part of the hearing concerned Robert's assertion that he had returned to the family home to look after his father and later supported his mother as she grew older. His siblings offered a different account of everyday life in the house. Marina, a senior accountant who had worked in the US and Canada, told the court that she was shocked by the condition of her mother and the property when she visited in 2016. She questioned how Robert could claim to have been providing care when, according to her, Irene was still responsible for much of the household work.Marina also described her brother spending long periods watching films in the living room while their mother dealt with cooking, cleaning and other domestic responsibilities. Her husband, Stephen Bennett, provided further evidence, recalling occasions when he had helped with household repairs despite Robert living at the property. Reportedly, Robert maintained that he had contributed to his parents' household and pointed to giving his mother around £50 each week towards expenses. He also referred to preparing mashed potatoes for meals as an example of his involvement.Recorder McDonald did not consider these contributions sufficient to establish that Robert had been caring for his mother. He said the evidence suggested Irene continued to manage the household, including washing, cooking and cleaning, while also helping to look after her grandchildren. The judge found that Robert had not provided the level of support he claimed, either to his mother or to his father.Judge rejected the inheritance claim and ordered him to leaveIn dismissing Robert's case, the judge said his allegations about the promises made by his parents were unsupported by the available records. He was particularly critical of the suggestion that Victor had intended to send Irene back to Finland without any financial provision. The court also considered the consequences of allowing Robert to inherit the entire property. Such an outcome would have left no significant assets available for distribution between his siblings, despite the absence of evidence that their mother had intended to favour one child over the others.The ruling required Robert to vacate the South Woodford property within 28 days and remove his belongings. The court also made a financial order totalling £265,000, covering legal expenses and charges relating to his continued occupation of the house.Of that amount, £90,000 was awarded towards the legal costs incurred by his siblings and the administrator of the estate. The remaining £175,000 represented mesne profits, a legal term for compensation payable for occupying property without the right to do so, covering the period after he had been asked to leave following his mother's death.His legal battle could have consumed his share of the inheritanceThe proceedings had continued for more than eight years, leaving the administration of Irene's estate unresolved long after her death. The judge said the dispute needed to end, particularly given the time already spent dealing with the property and the competing claims. The court also heard that Robert's siblings had previously offered him a settlement that would have allowed him to receive 62.5% of the property's value. That proposal was not accepted, and the case proceeded to trial. Under the outcome, each of the three children remained entitled to one-third of the estate. However, the legal expenses and occupation-related payment could substantially reduce the value of the share Robert might otherwise have received.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available court reports and media coverage. The Times of India has not independently verified the claims made by the parties.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
